proceedings.title: Writ petition under Article 226

workflow.text: Answer the maintainability questions: the forum, the alternative remedy, the delay and the parties.
Analyse the alternative remedy and why it is not adequate.
Set out the fundamental rights and the judicial review grounds.
Draft the writ petition from the record.
Review the draft, citations and grounding.

intakeQuestions: Which fundamental or legal right is violated, and by which act?
Is there an alternative statutory remedy? Why is it not adequate?
Is the petition within a reasonable time of the impugned act?
Is the impugned act administrative, quasi-judicial or legislative?
Are the parties and the authority correctly named?
evidence: The representation and its reply, if any
The statutory remedy and the order under it

terms.meaning: Whether the court can hear the petition at all: the forum, the remedy, the delay and the parties.
A statutory route the petitioner could use instead of the writ.
The court's review of an act for legality, reasonableness and procedure, not its merits.

intakeQuestions: Is the respondent a State or an instrumentality?
Is there a disputed question of fact?

terms.meaning: The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction for the enforcement of fundamental rights.

proceedings.title: Review and curative petition
provisions: Order XLVII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
unmappedParts: Review petition (the document catalogue has no review petition template yet)

workflow.text: Analyse the judgment and the ground of review.
Draft the review petition from the record.
Review the draft against the record.

intakeQuestions: What is the error apparent on the face of the record?
Was the point raised and decided?
What is the date of the judgment?
Is a curative petition the next step?
evidence: The earlier review order, if any

terms.meaning: A petition to the same court to correct an error apparent on the face of the record.
